newsitem.title: ITALY: Bank Italy seen selling marks for lire - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Bank Italy seen selling marks for lire - dealers.

text.p: The Bank of Italy sold marks for lire above 1,003 lire several times on the foreign currency markets on Tuesday, dealers said.
The lira was quoted at 1,003.20/3.60 per mark at 1057 GMT after touching a session low of 1,003.90.
"The only one selling marks this morning is the Bank of Italy," said one dealer who said he had seen intervention between 1,003 and 1,004 lire.
"These are just the usual sales, they're nothing special," he added.
The lira fell after Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher said delaying European economic and monetary union (EMU) would be the only option if Bonn failed to meet EMU criteria.
